text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between Chelsea and Crystal Palace at Stamford Bridge!

Languishing inside the bottom half of the table after being beaten 2-1 by Wolves last weekend, Chelsea now return to headquarters, where they have won their last two Premier League home games - as many as in the previous 17.

The Blues may have just lost for an eighth time in 18 top-flight fixtures under Mauricio Pochettino, but the ex-Tottenham coach boasts a particularly impressive record against today's visitors: he has won 11 of 13 league meetings with Crystal Palace - more than against any other opponent.
Making the short trip to West London, Crystal Palace have posted just one victory in seven league matches following back-to-back draws with Manchester City and Brighton.
The Eagles occupy 15th position in the table, four points adrift of their hosts.

However, history suggests closing that gap today may be a tall order: Palace’s 11 consecutive Premier League defeats against Chelsea is their longest losing run against any opponent in their entire history - and they have also lost on each of their last six visits to Stamford Bridge, failing to even score in the last four.
Chelsea make no less than five changes to the XI that lined up against Wolves, with Caicedo, Mudryk, Badiashile, Maatsen and Sunday's goalscorer Nkunku all brought into the side.
Cole Palmer and Raheem Sterling must serve suspensions; Thiago Silva and Broja are both demoted to the bench, while Lesley Ugochukwu misses out entirely.
Meanwhile, Roy Hodgson opts for just one change to the Crystal Palace team that drew 1-1 with Brighton: Hughes is benched, as Eze starts for the first time in over a month.
Former Chelsea youth-teamer Olise therefore starts in the supporting cast for lone striker Mateta.
The teams emerge from the tunnel at Stamford Bridge, and kick-off in this Premier League contest is now just moments away!
Crystal Palace kick off, and we are under way in London!
Although 26-year-old Nkunku makes his first start today, Chelsea have still named their youngest-ever Premier League starting XI (23 years, 21 days).
It's also the youngest side named by any top-flight team since Manchester Utd against Crystal Palace in May 2017.

Palace enjoy some early possession inside Chelsea's half, but it comes to very little until Olise's run past Colwill on the right is ended by the Chelsea defender pulling back his opponent and conceding a 20-yard free-kick.
On the right side of the box, just a few feet outside the area, Eze steps up to the free-kick Olise won and then ripples the side-netting of Petrovic's goal.
It was a good effort, but the Chelsea goalkeeper was not too concerned.
Rather hopefully, Andersen steps forward and tries his luck from over 25 yards out, shooting from a central position but seeing his attempt comfortably saved by Petrovic.

OFF THE LINE! At the end of a quick counter initiated by Mudryk, Maatsen slips through into the area and guides the ball under Henderson - however, Mitchell comes to Crystal Palace's rescue! The full-back sprints back to clear the ball away from near his goal line - that's a close escape for the Eagles!
While Chelsea are winless in four Premier League home London derbies, Palace have won just one of their last 13 capital-city contests - beating West Ham 4-3 in April.
Away from home, they’re winless in seven.

CHELSEA LEAD! Mudryk prods home from close range, putting the home side 1-0 in front! At the second attempt, Nkunku slips a ball through to the overlapping Gusto on the left, and the latter's sharp cutback finds Chelsea's Ukrainian winger alone in the six-yard box! Henderson had no chance!
After sprinting into the left side of the area, Gusto stays cool upon receiving the ball and picks out Mudryk with a low cross.
Chelsea are in hot pursuit of a second goal now: Gallagher whips over a free-kick from the left, but Nkunku can't control his header, which flies wildly over the crossbar.

Just five yards from his own goal, Gusto makes another vital intervention, as he lunges in to beat Ayew to the ball and cut out a dangerous cross from the right by Olise, who has been Palace's most threatening player so far.
Olise is continuing to cause his old club problems, and this time his curling cross picks out Mateta at the back post.
The big striker's cutback is hacked away from danger, though, and Chelsea survive another scare.
SAVE! Jackson guides a clever backheel into Mudryk's path on the edge of the area, and the latter sprints through on goal, looking for all the world like he'll net his second goal of the game.
However, Henderson is quickly off his line to make a sharp stop at close range! Good goalkeeping!
Chelsea have had around two-thirds of the ball so far, although the game has not been played entirely in Crystal Palace's half - far from it.
It's been an open game, but the hosts have an important advantage and the Eagles have a mountain to climb.

Shortly after Jackson fails to make the most of a promising position inside the area - pulling the ball across the six-yard box to no-one in particular rather than shooting - Nkunku topples to the turf and claims a penalty.
Both the referee and the VAR are disinterested, though.
Chelsea are building play from the back when Mateta steals the ball and then feeds Olise on the left.
The latter then tries a first-time shot from 20 yards, but it is charged down by the first blue-shirted defender in front of him.
After Palace fail to make the most of a free-kick at the other end, a typically rapid burst by Mudryk turns momentum on its head and ultimately wins Chelsea a corner on the left.

The home side are still bossing the ball, passing patiently around in midfield while seeking an opening, but Palace don't mind their opponents having more possession - they can counter-attack at speed.
Following a sweeping switch of play from left to right, a swift passing move sees Maatsen advance towards the area and have a shot partly blocked behind.
Chelsea are increasingly dangerous now - having Nkunku to play off has apparently lightened the burden on their front men.
A lovely switch of direction by Olise opens up a yard or two of space by the right touchline, but Lerma just mistimes his run and is immediately flagged for offside.
It's been a fairly quiet shift for Petrovic so far.
This game is becoming quite comfortable for Chelsea to dictate, as Palace sit off a little.
Approaching half-time, Pochettino will be by far the happier manager.
Gusto's impressive display continues, as the French full-back steals the ball from Ayew deep inside his own half, then is involved in a quick-counter attack up the other end.

Gallagher curls in a high free-kick from just inside Palace's half, and his delivery is just too strong for Disasi to bring down and either head towards goal or nod it on for one of several team-mates gathered in the area.
Crystal Palace are looking a little lost as the first half reaches its conclusion, they've faded out of contention after starting well enough.
Still, they only trail by one.

PALACE PULL LEVEL! Killing the ball with his first touch and then sweeping it home with is second, Olise clinically makes it 1-1 at Stamford Bridge! On the left, Ayew is left in acres of space to weigh up his options, and his flat delivery beats everyone in a packed box before landing on Olise's chest.
That's a superb finish at the back post, and out of the blue, Crystal Palace are back on terms!
Ayew looks up, assesses his options, then picks out Olise with a precise lofted throughball from the left.
HALF-TIME: CHELSEA 1-1 CRYSTAL PALACE
Stunned by a last-gasp leveller, Chelsea's young side traipse down the tunnel with no advantage gained from a first-half showing of some promise.

Having suffered without the ball for long spells, Crystal Palace seemed set to trail at the break, as the lively Mudryk struck their hosts' opener early on, before Henderson made a crucial save from the same player soon after.
However, the Eagles produced a moment of magic when Ayew and Olise combined in stoppage time.
That leaves this London derby finely balanced at the interval, with everything to play for during the second half.
Chelsea have now conceded 59 Premier League goals in 2023 - the most league goals they've shipped in a single year since 1991.
Meanwhile, Olise has now had a hand in 10 goals during his last 15 top-flight starts.
Perhaps, given their hosts' defensive woes, Palace's losing streak against the Blues can finally end today?
Chelsea kick off, and we are back under way at Stamford Bridge!
Eze twice leaves Chelsea's defence scrambling to clear the ball, as he weaves some magic on the left side of the Blues' area before sending in a couple of dangerous deliveries.
Finally, Maatsen hammers the ball clear.

After a brief pause in proceedings for both Gusto and Andersen to receive treatment - the latter having picked up a knock in an aerial challenge - the game resumes, with the two players back in their positions.
Mitchell gifts the ball to Maatsen in midfield, almost obliging Lerma to commit a foul to cover the danger.
Fortunately for the Crystal Palace full-back, nothing comes of the subsequent set-piece.
Arriving late on Olise from behind, Caicedo becomes the first player on either side booked today.
He also concedes a free-kick around 25 yards from goal.
Eze steps up to the free-kick won by Olise, but his dipping effort from a central position is sent flashing past the left-hand post without seriously troubling Petrovic.
SAVE! Mateta picks up the ball on the right flank, then beats two Chelsea defenders far too easily despite his lack of express pace.
Taking his chance to shoot low and hard from a tight angle, the Palace striker forces Petrovic to tip the ball behind at his near post!
JUST OVER! Mateta comes close again, as a looping ball is flicked on by Richards' header inside the box and lands at his feet.
However, he steers the ball over the crossbar from close range, and Chelsea breathe another sigh of relief! Palace are building some momentum now!
Pochettino can sense his side have started this second half without the required focus, so changes are inevitable: first, Colwill is replaced by Thiago Silva.
Lavia is also welcomed onto the pitch for his long-delayed Chelsea debut, with Maatsen making way.

It's end-to-end at the Bridge! First, Nkunku prompts Henderson to palm away a dangerous cross flashed across Palace's six-yard box; then, Eze's deflected shot from the edge of Chelsea's area is gathered by Petrovic.
Chelsea are regaining a modicum of control now, as Palace are forced a few yards back.
It looks like the hosts' substitutions have brought about a change on either flank, with Gusto and Disasi filling in.
Gallagher decides against pulling the trigger from 25 yards, and Chelsea's patient passing around the perimeter of Palace's box ultimately comes to nothing.
The home fans are now growing a little impatient - their team is totally dominating possession but remain level at 1-1.
Now Palace probe around the opposition area, and Ayew eventually releases a low cross from the left that is cleared away by Chelsea's rather nervy defence.
Ayew dwells on the ball for too long in an advanced position, failing to release Mitchell.
He then runs into traffic on the edge of the area, so the visitors are obliged to build again.
Two more changes for Chelsea: Nkunku's full debut ends early, as Madueke jogs on to the pitch as his replacement.
Opening goalscorer Mudryk also departs, with Broja sent on to aid Jackson up front.
After a prolonged Palace attack is ended, Madueke sprints away on the counter.
Richards brings the young winger down at the second attempt, earning himself a merited yellow card.
MISS! Jackson spurns a sitter! Caicedo and Gallagher combine to split the Palace defence, and Chelsea's Senegalese striker is sent clean through on goal.
However, Henderson dives at his feet, and his hurried shot is guided just wide of the right-hand post! So close!

CHELSEA STRIKE AGAIN! Arriving unmarked at the back post, Jackson slots past Henderson to make up for his miss just moments ago! A cross from the right by Thiago Silva is deflected into the striker's path and he makes no mistake! But wait, the VAR will take a look at this - was he offside?

NO GOAL! Chelsea are denied a second goal by an offside ruling! It's heartbreak for the Blues and particularly for Jackson, who had picked himself up following a terrible miss and seemingly scored the winner! It stays 1-1!
Palace's first substitution: Schlupp comes on for Ayew.
Madueke is booked for a coming-together with Mitchell by the touchline.
Mitchell is also shown a yellow card for his part in the confrontation with Madueke.

SAVE! Released on the right side of the box by Schlupp, Olise has one shot blocked before firing the follow-up low and hard towards the near post: Petrovic gets down to make a crucial save! It's just a corner for Palace! This game can still go either way!

Another brilliant throughball by Thiago Silva - this time from deep - picks out the run of Broja, who takes the ball down perfectly with his first touch but then fires into the side-netting with a rather rash finish from the left side of Palace's area.
Richards heads away an inswinging corner deep inside his own area, then Andersen nods it further clear and Palace quickly set off on a lightning-quick counter.
Eze eventually runs into too much traffic in a central position, though, and Chelsea escape.

PENALTY FOR CHELSEA? Long after the incident actually unfolded, the referee is called across to the pitchside monitor! It seems Eze tripped Madueke at that last Chelsea corner, and it looks like the Blues will soon have a spot-kick!
PENALTY CONFIRMED! The referee concurs with his VAR colleagues! Chelsea will have a great chance to win it from 12 yards - it's a penalty!

CHELSEA LEAD 2-1! The hosts have a precious lead, with just one minute of the 90 remaining! Madueke steps up to the spot-kick he won himself, sending Henderson the wrong way with a composed penalty-kick into the bottom-left corner! Surely that's the winner!?
Stunned by going behind, Palace make another change: it's a rare chance for Matheus Franca now; Lerma comes off.
Pochettino plays his final card in the second minute of at least eight added for stoppages.
Badiashile makes way for young Gilchrist.
Lacking sufficient pace to seriously trouble Petrovic, Olise's shot from the right side of the box is saved in the bottom-right corner by Chelsea's stand-in goalkeeper.
Time is running out for Palace now.
With the pressure intense to produce results, Pochettino oversteps the line and is booked by the referee.
Bouncing back from last week's defeat at Wolves would ease the Chelsea coach's woes somewhat.
Can his side hold on here?
Gallagher is also shown a late yellow card for dissent.
Jackson is caught offside again, and Crystal Palace have a free-kick deep inside their own territory.
Will they be able to force one more opening, or is it already too late to find a second equaliser?
FULL-TIME: CHELSEA 2-1 CRYSTAL PALACE
Stealing all three points with a late penalty coolly converted by substitute Madueke, Chelsea recover from letting a lead slip to beat Crystal Palace 2-1 at Stamford Bridge.
A 12th straight league defeat of the Eagles matches their record run of victories against any club, and more importantly eases the pressure on Pochettino's young squad.
The hosts had most of the ball throughout, but Eze and Olise were often a threat for Palace, with the latter sweeping in their equaliser shortly before the break after Mudryk had opened the scoring.

Chelsea found a way to win it, though, and will wrap up their 2023 schedule by visiting Luton Town at the weekend; meanwhile, Palace - who have now conceded in the 80th minute or beyond in six of their past eight Premier League matches - host local rivals Brentford on Saturday.
That's all from today's live coverage, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!
